title: Vocabulary file
description: One fixed word list, e.g. classes or damage types. Every data file and every generated card may only use term ids from these lists. Constraint fields (classes, allowed, excluded, requires, min_tier) bind generated cards; on researched units a break is only reported as 'atypical'. Rarity fields (rarity, class_rarity) only weight the generator's choices.

group.description: core = named in the brief; supporting = added to make the core lists work.

tie_breaks.description: Rules for coding source units when two or more terms seem to fit equally well: which one to pick. Written from the calibration pilot, where coders disagreed. A term of another list is written '<list>:<id>'.

terms.description: The terms the rule chooses between.

rule.description: Which term to pick, and how to tell, in plain words.

replaces.description: Term ids of earlier word-list versions that this term takes over (merged or renamed). Data still using them must move to this term.

examples.description: Reference examples from the research, paraphrased.

rarity.description: How readily the generator offers this term (see the rarity list).

source_only.description: Recorded for research; never rolled by the generator.

rank.description: Order on a scale (speed, size, cost, armour...).

classes.description: The unit classes this term is physically possible for. A class left out is a hard ban: the generator never rolls the term for it. This is how 'aircraft don't get tracks' is enforced. A class for which the term is possible but unusual stays in this list and gets a rarity in class_rarity.

class_rarity.description: Rarity of this term for particular classes, used instead of 'rarity' when the unit is of that class; classes not listed use 'rarity'. Every key must be in 'classes'. This is how cross-overs such as a flamethrower on an aircraft stay rare and appear only at high spice. A faction's one-step bonus for favoured parts does not apply to it.

allowed.description: Whitelist of terms this one may combine with on the same unit, keyed by vocabulary id. Checked both ways.

excluded.description: Terms this one may not combine with on the same unit, keyed by vocabulary id.

requires.description: What the unit must also have for this term to make sense.

min_tier.description: Lowest tier that may use this term.

uses_key.description: Ability kinds and mobility traits: true if it is a button that counts toward the tier's key budget.

pattern.description: Mobility traits: the mechanic pattern a key-bound trait stands for.

target_type.description: Mobility: what kind of target a unit moving this way is.

strong_vs.description: Damage types: what this damage is good against (typed links to what the target is).

immune.description: Damage types: targets this damage does nothing to.

max_keys.description: Tiers: most buttons a unit may have, signature included.

source_rule.description: How to code a source unit with this term: what in the source decides it. For tiers, how a game's tech level maps to the tier.

favoured.description: Faction flavours: term ids the flavour leans toward, keyed by vocabulary id.

avoided.description: Faction flavours: term ids held back at low spice, keyed by vocabulary id.

favoured_weight.description: Faction flavours: how much more likely favoured terms are.

severity.description: Balance flags: block = never on a rolled card; warn = shown as a hint.

brings.description: What this term adds to a card's matchups when rolled (filled in with the generator, Phase 2).
